prompt :
Create an ultra-realistic premium editorial portrait using the PROVIDED PERSON REFERENCE IMAGE as the STRICT IDENTITY REFERENCE.

The supplied reference image controls the identity, facial appearance, hairstyle, hair texture, skin tone, facial proportions, body proportions, and recognizable characteristics of the MAIN PERSON.

IMPORTANT:

Preserve the exact recognizable identity of the supplied person.

Do not replace the face with a generic model.

Do not redesign the person's facial features.

Do not change the person's age, skin tone, face shape, eye shape, nose, lips, eyebrows, or distinctive characteristics.

Create ONE SINGLE VERTICAL COMPOSITE IMAGE divided into TWO HALVES by a dramatic irregular vertical torn-paper transition.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

LEFT HALF — REAL PHOTOGRAPH

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

On the LEFT side, show the supplied person as a completely photorealistic, high-end fashion portrait.

The person should look exactly like the supplied reference identity.

Pose:

- confident relaxed standing pose

- upper-body / three-quarter portrait

- face turned slightly toward the camera

- calm, confident editorial expression

- natural posture

- realistic human anatomy

Wardrobe:

Create a sophisticated modern fashion outfit inspired by the target image:

a fitted black top underneath an elegant warm rust / burnt-orange blazer or jacket.

Preserve realistic fabric texture, stitching, folds, shadows and natural clothing behavior.

HAIR:

Maintain the person's reference hairstyle and hair characteristics as accurately as possible.

Individual hair strands must be visible.

Natural volume and realistic movement.

LIGHTING:

Soft natural daylight.

Subtle cinematic highlights.

Realistic facial shadows.

Natural skin texture.

Professional fashion photography lighting.

BACKGROUND:

Modern contemporary architectural environment with a large glass-and-steel building facade.

Tall vertical windows and structural lines behind the subject.

Soft realistic depth of field.

Clean urban editorial atmosphere.

The LEFT HALF must look like a genuine professional photograph.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

RIGHT HALF — HAND-DRAWN COMIC VERSION

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

On the RIGHT side, recreate the SAME PERSON as a sophisticated monochrome hand-drawn fashion illustration.

The illustrated person must clearly resemble the exact person from the supplied reference image.

Preserve:

- same face identity

- same hairstyle

- same facial proportions

- same approximate pose

- same body proportions

- same clothing silhouette

Transform ONLY the visual medium into a detailed black-and-white editorial comic illustration.

Illustration style:

- hand-drawn ink artwork

- sophisticated fashion illustration

- clean black outlines

- subtle grayscale shading

- realistic anatomy

- elegant sketchbook quality

- expressive facial details

- carefully drawn hair strands

- professional graphic-novel / fashion-comic aesthetic

Do NOT make it childish.

Do NOT make it cartoonish.

Do NOT use anime style.

Do NOT use exaggerated comic proportions.

The illustrated person should feel like a high-fashion black-and-white graphic novel character based directly on the real person.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CENTER TRANSITION — TORN PAPER

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Create a dramatic irregular VERTICAL TORN-PAPER DIVISION between the real photograph and the illustration.

The split should NOT be a clean straight line.

It must look like REAL PAPER being torn vertically from the top to the bottom.

Create:

- irregular jagged edges

- uneven ripped-paper fibers

- realistic paper thickness

- subtle white paper fibers

- tiny torn fragments

- slight shadow along the ripped edge

- natural imperfect tearing

- convincing physical paper texture

The torn edge should reveal a clear transition from:

PHOTOREALISTIC PERSON → HAND-DRAWN ILLUSTRATION.

The transition must feel physically layered and believable.

Do not use a simple digital split-screen effect.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ILLUSTRATION DETAILS

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Add tasteful hand-drawn doodle elements around the illustrated half, similar to a creative fashion sketchbook:

small cloud

small stars

small heart

simple coffee cup

small vintage camera

tiny decorative sparkles

These elements must be black-and-white hand-drawn ink doodles.

Keep them subtle and aesthetically balanced.

Do not overcrowd the image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

MATCHING BETWEEN BOTH HALVES

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The REAL and ILLUSTRATED versions must represent the SAME PERSON.

Their:

- face

- hairstyle

- pose

- clothing

- body proportions

- overall silhouette

must visually correspond across the torn-paper boundary.

The left side is REAL.

The right side is the HAND-DRAWN artistic interpretation of that same person.

Make the transition look intentional and seamless.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

VISUAL STYLE

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Luxury fashion editorial.

Creative advertising campaign.

Premium magazine photography.

Photorealistic + hand-drawn mixed-media artwork.

Modern artistic portrait.

Sophisticated minimal composition.

High-end visual storytelling.

The final image should look like a professionally designed fashion campaign rather than an ordinary AI-generated image.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CAMERA

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Eye-level camera.

Straight-on perspective.

Medium / three-quarter portrait.

Natural lens perspective.

No fisheye distortion.

No extreme wide-angle distortion.

Sharp focus on the main subject.

Realistic depth of field.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

COLOR

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

LEFT SIDE:

Natural full color.

Warm realistic skin tones.

Burnt-orange / rust clothing.

Neutral architectural background.

RIGHT SIDE:

Strict black-and-white / grayscale.

White paper background.

Black ink outlines.

Soft gray shading.

Keep the two visual worlds clearly distinguishable.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

OUTPUT QUALITY

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Ultra-photorealistic.

Extremely detailed.

Professional editorial quality.

Natural skin pores.

Realistic hair strands.

Detailed clothing texture.

Highly detailed ink illustration.

Fine paper fibers.

Accurate anatomy.

Clean composition.

Premium commercial advertising quality.

TARGET OUTPUT RESOLUTION:

16K ULTRA HIGH RESOLUTION

15360 × 8640 pixels

approximately 132.7 million pixels.

If the image-generation system cannot natively generate 15360 × 8640 pixels, generate at the highest available resolution while preserving maximum detail, composition, identity consistency, and fine texture, optimized for high-quality 16K upscaling.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

STRICT NEGATIVE PROMPT

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

different person, changed identity, generic face, face replacement, face swap, identity drift, altered facial structure, different hairstyle, different hair color, different skin tone, different age, inconsistent face, two different people, duplicate person, extra person, extra limbs, extra fingers, deformed hands, bad anatomy, distorted body, unrealistic proportions, plastic skin, wax skin, CGI, 3D render, anime, childish cartoon, low-quality cartoon, colorful illustration, straight split line, clean digital divider, smooth transition, messy torn paper, fake paper edge, excessive doodles, cluttered background, distorted architecture, blurry face, low resolution, oversharpening, excessive HDR, artificial skin, unrealistic clothing, random text, typography, logo, watermark, signature, captions.

Character reference sheet for consistent AI generation — multiple angles, outfit details, hair, face, hands, and accessories in one visual guide.

Created with @magnific 
prompt ;
Create a highly detailed, professional CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT / CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET using the uploaded reference image as the ONLY source for the subject's identity.

IMPORTANT IDENTITY PRESERVATION RULE:
Use the uploaded reference image strictly for the subject's true identity. Preserve the exact recognizable facial identity, facial structure, proportions, eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, cheeks, jawline, chin, forehead, skin characteristics, natural asymmetry, hairline and all distinctive facial features.

Do NOT beautify, idealize, stylize, redesign, or replace the person's face.
Do NOT change the person's ethnicity, age appearance, gender presentation, facial proportions, or recognizable identity.
Do NOT create a lookalike or a generic model.
The subject must remain clearly recognizable as the same person throughout every panel.

If the reference image is male, keep the subject male.
If the reference image is female, keep the subject female.
Follow the natural appearance of the reference image exactly.

Create ONE clean professional character reference sheet / model sheet containing multiple views and detailed visual references of the SAME PERSON.

OVERALL STYLE:
Professional film/animation character-development reference board.
Photorealistic studio photography.
High-end fashion/editorial photography quality.
Neutral studio background.
Clean controlled studio lighting.
Realistic skin texture.
Natural pores and subtle facial imperfections.
Accurate anatomy.
Consistent proportions.
No fantasy styling.
No cartoon or illustration appearance.
No excessive retouching.
No beauty-filter effect.

SHEET COMPOSITION:

Organize the final image into a clean professional multi-panel reference sheet similar to a production character sheet.

SECTION 1 — FULL BODY VIEWS:
Include:
1. Full-body FRONT view — standing naturally, facing directly toward camera.
2. Full-body SIDE PROFILE view — true 90-degree side profile.
3. Full-body BACK view — facing completely away from camera.
4. Optional 3/4 full-body view if space allows.

Keep the exact same person, same body proportions, same hairstyle, same facial identity, same clothing and same physical characteristics across all views.

The full-body poses should be neutral and relaxed:
- arms naturally positioned
- feet naturally aligned
- upright posture
- no exaggerated pose
- no action pose

SECTION 2 — HEAD / FACE ANGLES:
Create detailed head-and-shoulders portraits showing the same person's face from multiple angles:

1. Straight FRONT portrait
2. 3/4 LEFT view
3. TRUE LEFT PROFILE
4. 3/4 RIGHT view
5. TRUE RIGHT PROFILE
6. Slight HIGH ANGLE looking downward
7. Slight LOW ANGLE looking upward
8. BACK OF HEAD / HAIR view if useful

Every face angle must maintain EXACT facial identity and consistent anatomy.

The eyes, nose, lips, jawline, cheekbones, eyebrows, ears, hairline and facial proportions must remain consistent between every portrait.

SECTION 3 — BACK / HAIR REFERENCE:
Include a clear rear view of the head and hair showing:
- hairstyle
- hair length
- hair density
- natural hair texture
- hairline
- back-of-head shape

Do not invent a different hairstyle unless it is necessary to accurately represent what is visible in the reference.

SECTION 4 — CLOTHING / OUTFIT REFERENCE:
Show detailed close-up crops of the clothing and accessories.

Include useful detail panels such as:
- fabric texture
- seams
- stitching
- folds
- waistband
- collar
- sleeves
- buttons/zippers
- shoes
- jewelry/accessories if present

Keep the exact same outfit across all views.

SECTION 5 — SKIN / FACIAL DETAIL:
Include several macro-detail crops where appropriate:
- realistic skin texture / pores
- eye detail
- eyebrow detail
- lips
- distinctive facial features
- any visible freckles, moles, scars, marks or natural skin characteristics

These details must come directly from the reference subject and must NOT be artificially invented.

SECTION 6 — HANDS / SHOES / ACCESSORIES:
If visible and relevant, include clean close-up reference crops of:
- hands
- fingers
- shoes
- jewelry
- glasses
- watches
- bags
- other distinctive accessories

Keep all details consistent with the main character.

CONSISTENCY RULE:
ALL PANELS MUST REPRESENT THE EXACT SAME PERSON.

Maintain absolute consistency in:
- facial identity
- facial geometry
- body proportions
- height/build
- hairstyle
- hair color
- skin tone
- eye color
- eyebrows
- clothing
- accessories
- shoes
- age appearance

Do not allow individual panels to drift into different faces or different body types.

CAMERA / PHOTOGRAPHY:
Professional studio photography.
Full-frame camera look.
Natural perspective.
Approximately 50–85mm equivalent portrait perspective for face shots.
Natural perspective for full-body shots.
Sharp facial detail.
High dynamic range.
Soft, controlled studio illumination.
Subtle realistic shadows.
Neutral white/gray studio background.
Consistent lighting direction across the sheet.

LAYOUT:
Create a polished editorial contact-sheet layout with clearly separated rectangular panels.

Use small professional section labels such as:
FULL BODY VIEWS
HEAD ANGLES
BACK / HAIR
DETAILS
FACE
CLOTHING
SHOES

Use thin clean dividers between panels.
Balanced spacing.
Professional production-design presentation.
Minimal typography.
No decorative graphics that distract from the character.

IMPORTANT:
The reference image is the identity anchor.
Do NOT copy the exact composition of the reference image if it conflicts with the uploaded subject.
Instead, reproduce the REFERENCE SHEET FORMAT, organization, panel logic, photography style and level of detail while replacing the example subject with the person from the uploaded reference.

The final result should look like a professionally photographed CHARACTER REFERENCE / MODEL SHEET created for a film, animation, VFX, game, fashion or AI character-production pipeline.

ULTRA-REALISM REQUIREMENTS:
Photorealistic human.
Natural skin pores.
Individual hair strands.
Realistic eyes with natural reflections.
Realistic fabric behavior.
Physically accurate anatomy.
Natural hands and fingers.
Correct facial symmetry/asymmetry.
No plastic skin.
No CGI appearance.
No artificial beauty filter.
No warped anatomy.
No duplicated features.
No inconsistent face between panels.
No extra fingers.
No distorted hands.
No floating objects.
No text artifacts.
No random logos.
No watermark.

FINAL PRIORITY:
1. EXACT IDENTITY PRESERVATION
2. CONSISTENT CHARACTER ACROSS ALL PANELS
3. ACCURATE ANATOMY AND PROPORTIONS
4. PHOTOREALISTIC QUALITY
5. PROFESSIONAL REFERENCE-SHEET LAYOUT
6. HIGH-DETAIL VISUAL REFERENCES

Use the uploaded image as the sole identity reference and generate the complete professional character reference sheet.

part 2: "Attention Is All You Need" by Vaswani et al.

arguably the most consequential paper in modern AI.

- the authors cover the original Transformer's computation and information flow. 

- scaled dot-product attention, softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V, where d_k is the query/key width. the authors scale the logits to counteract large dot products that can produce small softmax gradients.

- separate learned Q/K/V projections for each attention head, followed by per-head weighted aggregation, concatenation, and a learned output projection.

- cross-attention uses decoder queries against encoder keys/values, conditioning predictions on contextualized source representations.

- masking future-position logits before softmax and shifting target embeddings by one position. training parallelizes across known target positions; generation still depends on previous outputs.

- position-wise FFNs transform representations without mixing tokens. the original post-norm architecture applies residual addition before layer normalization.

- sinusoidal positional encodings supply positional information. for any fixed offset, the shifted encoding is a linear function of the original encoding.

- full-sequence self-attention mixing, excluding projections, costs O(n²d), versus O(nd²) for dense recurrence, where n is sequence length and d is representation width. direct connections shorten dependency paths, while all-pairs attention introduces quadratic sequence-length scaling.

- in the authors' English-to-German development experiments, label smoothing improved BLEU despite worse perplexity; varying head count at fixed total attention width did not produce monotonic BLEU gains.

the big model scaled the same encoder-decoder architecture to 16 attention heads, a model width of 1,024, and a feed-forward width of 4,096. the authors report 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German newstest2014 test set after 3.5 days on eight NVIDIA P100 GPUs. they averaged the last 20 checkpoints for evaluation. the score exceeded the strongest ensemble listed in Table 2 by over two BLEU.

why this paper was so consequential:

- the authors replaced sequence-aligned recurrence with attention. training could process known sequence positions in parallel, with shorter paths between distant tokens than recurrent models. coauthor Jakob Uszkoreit linked this parallel computation to better use of GPUs and TPUs.

- in 2018, GPT paired a Transformer decoder with generative pretraining; BERT paired a bidirectional Transformer encoder with masked-language-model pretraining. both learned representations from unlabeled text that researchers could reuse across downstream tasks. by October 2020, Google reported using BERT in almost every English query.

- GPT-3's authors evaluated the model using instructions or examples in its context, without task-specific gradient updates. they reported stronger few-shot performance as model size increased. Kaplan et al. quantified empirical relationships between language-model loss, parameters, training data, and compute, and analyzed how to allocate a training budget.

- for the original ChatGPT launch in November 2022, OpenAI adapted a GPT-3.5-family model using dialogue demonstrations and reinforcement learning from human feedback.

- researchers also adapted Transformers to other kinds of data. ViT processed images as sequences of patch embeddings. DiT used Transformers to denoise latent image patches, and the 2024 Sora research model used a diffusion Transformer over spacetime latent patches. these systems used Transformer components for image recognition, image generation, and video generation.

- systems researchers also optimized Transformer training and inference. Megatron-LM partitioned attention and MLP computation across GPUs. FlashAttention used tiling and recomputation to reduce HBM traffic for exact attention. vLLM used PagedAttention so a sequence's KV-cache blocks could occupy noncontiguous GPU memory. Hugging Face Transformers packaged model variants and pretrained weights behind common interfaces. OpenAI's 2020 API launch offered private-beta access to models from the GPT-3 family.

Apparently people are also angry that I posted about Luma and played around with AI recently...

So again:

1) Luma was a nice little hobby thing on the side. Wicked is my main gig, obviously! Luma is a project I had in mind for almost a decade, built 2 prototypes of it already over the years (it's the project I showed to Oculus back in 2016 or so) and then did a gamejam where I finally solved the issues I got stuck on before.

It was the first game I was able to make with my 8 year old son. He and I played Minecraft together a lot and we talked about how one could make an even better game and that's how Luma jumped back into my mind.

And honestly, it was delightful to be able to make something with him. As a parent, it's amazing if you find something that you and your kid both get excited about. Him coming home from school with dozens of ideas and overflowing with creative energy was one of the best moments for me this year.

So, sue me if you get offended that I spent a bunch of time with my son being creative together. I posted about it online because it's just a genuinely good game already!

Here try it yourself: https://t.co/Xu3yzKOs8p
It's really good! 👍

2) I already made my stance on AI clear. No, we're not using any generative AI stuff on Wicked and people who now claim otherwise are just making shit up in a ridiculous fashion. AI at this stage isn't good enough to create assets or any such thing, not at the quality standards we require at Moon. Any good gamedev knows what AI can do and what it can't. And if they don't, they're not taking their jobs seriously.

But of course we're using AI to help with tooling, bugfixes and so on, like everyone else is. We'd be stupid not to. It's a genuinely useful tool.

3) A similar thing happened with https://t.co/JolbgwKsO7 - It's a database I built for myself and for our team to keep track of things early on. But then it became clear that most gamers would get a huge kick out of it, so I released it.

And since then, I got tons and tons and tons of messages from industry folks and players that they're using it every day now. We had like 300k visitors on the site now and people are daily driving it to help them find new games.

What is there to get outraged about? How about we let people have fun and celebrate if they have a good time?

The internet can be exhausting these days...

If I were launching a fashion or beauty brand, I'd probably build the homepage like this.

Turns out GPT-6 Astra + Dreamina Seedance 2.5 is an actual pipeline.
First, create the same model/product character across completely different backgrounds in Dreamina. Then give those visuals to GPT-6 Astra and have it turn them into one continuous animated background.
The goal isn't really "AI video" - it's making the first few seconds of a brand website feel like a campaign film.
Dreamina's affordable generation cost makes it easy to test different scenes before committing to the final direction.
This is definitely the kind of homepage I'd stop scrolling for.
